rationale: Interim ten-person Barrett esophagus report used freeze-dried black raspberry and oxidative markers; no anxiety outcome in abstract. Shared investigators and protocol suggest a family with ranks 140 and 156, but individual overlap not explicitly verified.

Review describes raspberry leaf obstetric and enteric uses and other Rubus anxiety-related uses; review full reference list and species-specific primary linkage remain unavailable. An independently located Rubus brasiliensis rodent study is not verified as a cited study in this review.

Twenty completed Barrett patients received lyophilized black raspberry daily for 26 weeks, with baseline comparison and no untreated control; measured biomarkers and adverse events, not anxiety. Earlier interim and conference reports form a likely related protocol family.

Conference B34 describes twenty Barrett patients and six-month freeze-dried black raspberry intervention with biomarkers; no anxiety comparison. Same investigators, intervention, size and duration make rank 140 a likely shared study family; exact participant linkage not independently documented.

Snyder 2010 thesis tested individually quick-frozen whole red raspberries in healthy adults, but endpoints are oxidative biomarkers and a general symptom question rather than an anxiety measure; no parallel untreated chronic control. Same thesis as rank 184.
Duplicate of rank 158, University of Toronto thesis handle 1807/33687; full methods and instruments contain no specific anxiety assessment.

Uhrig 2014 thesis author abstract reports oral cancer survivors assigned black raspberry preparation or control, adherence and cancer-related biomarkers, not anxiety. Full thesis PDF is linked by repository but not reviewed here; do not infer its unexamined contents.

Xiao 2019 NCT02479035 crossover tested 0, 125 or 250 g frozen red raspberry in breakfast among 32 adults; primary body reports metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, no anxiety scale. Distinct registration and design from 2026 Xiao NCT03879213.

Smith 2019 randomized crossover in 20 young adults used freeze-dried black raspberry cereal bars, cranberry-extract bars and a reference bar; outcomes were postprandial metabolism, appetite and ex vivo oxidation, not anxiety.

Dobani 2021 reused samples from an earlier eleven-person 300 g homogenized raspberry feeding study for laboratory analysis; no anxiety outcome. It is not a second independently enrolled behavioral trial.

Fisher 2023 conference abstract studied laboratory outcomes using serum from 25 older adults after freeze-dried raspberry versus control; no human anxiety outcome. Similar investigators and intervention to NCT03879213 suggest possible overlap but registry link is not explicit.
